nh_holts_ledge.blurb: Holts Ledge is a winter ice crag on the slopes above the Dartmouth Skiway in Lyme, western New Hampshire, at roughly 1,700 feet. All ten climbs here are ice, running from WI3 to WI5 with most of them at the easier end and a few WI4 and WI5 lines above that. Two routes take two pitches; the rest are short single pitches. The lines sit close together along the right side of the ledge, the top is open so it is simple to walk between them, and trees allow rappelling. Flows on the left depend on snowmelt, while the ground-fed ones on the right hold up better in a dry winter. Expect sun on the ice for much of the day.

nh_cthulhu_boulder.blurb: Cthulhu Boulder is the largest of three boulders tucked into the woods of Town Forest South, in the Exeter area of southeastern New Hampshire. It holds ten problems from V0 up to V7, with the bulk sitting around V2 and V3, so there is something for newer boulderers and a couple of lines for strong ones. The landings are good and the boulder gets plenty of sun. A band of mineral runs across the north face. A smaller boulder sits about fifty feet away through the trees, and the group is off trail and hard to spot from a distance, so expect a little searching to find it.

nh_umbrella_boulder_the.blurb: At Rumney's Black Jack Boulders, the Umbrella Boulder is a large leaning block next to the main path; coming from the east, it is the first one with a clear traverse. It has ten problems and the spread is wide: a couple of easy ones, a middle group around V6 and V7, then a run of V9, V10 and two V13 lines. A well-chalked traverse across it makes a popular warm-up, with steeper straight-up lines above. In spring the ground at the base can turn to mud, so bring your own pads and take out any rubbish. Smaller boulders sit right beside it.

nh_lower_microwave_area.blurb: The Lower Microwave Area is the lowest and tallest of the three short cliffs that make up the Microwave Area in Pawtuckaway State Park, southern New Hampshire. The ten climbs here are mostly cracks on gear or top rope, with seven trad lines, a pair of boulder problems and one aid route. Free grades run from 5.6 to 5.10, so beginners to intermediate climbers can find leads, though the harder lines are scarce. The approach goes past Devil's Den and the boulder field, then up to a microwave reflector, with a faint climbers' trail dropping down from the summit to this wall.
